title: archiveSource cleanup can replace a real release result
definitionOfDone: A cleanup failure inside archiveSource can no longer replace the function's result: a test injects an rmSync that throws and asserts the ORIGINAL outcome still returns - both the success arm and the SOURCE_ARCHIVE_FAILED refusal arm, each asserted separately with its exact stable code.

The cleanup failure is reported rather than silently swallowed, following the pattern cleanRoots already established at supply-chain.mjs:184-188 - the archive removal still attempts, and its failure surfaces without becoming the return value.
The happy path is unchanged: the archive is still removed on both the success and refusal exits, asserted by checking the file is gone rather than by trusting the call was made.
A mutation drill proves the coverage is load-bearing: restoring the unguarded `finally { rmSync(...) }` turns a NAMED test red, and the drill is restored byte-exact and verified by hash.
Fresh pnpm test:integration exits 0 and the existing release-supply-chain tests stay green and unmodified.
taskRails: Copy the discipline cleanRoots already uses at supply-chain.mjs:184-188 rather than inventing a second cleanup convention in the same file. Two different cleanup patterns in one script is how the next half-fix happens.

The point is that the computed result survives. A test asserting only that no exception escaped is insufficient - assert the exact success value or the exact SOURCE_ARCHIVE_FAILED refusal is what the caller receives.
Do not touch cleanRoots, the release evidence format, or the refusal vocabulary. task-56117913 owns that surface and re-editing it would be a silent duplicate.
This file is plain .mjs with no type checking. Rely on the integration test rather than the compiler, and run the gate rather than reasoning about it.
Re-measure scripts/release/supply-chain.mjs:58-65 on current bytes before editing; preserve foreign work and commit only explicit owned paths.

implementationPlan.description: PRE-FLIGHT / RE-MEASURE WITHOUT WRITING BYTES. Record the task-start commit and `git status --short` for `scripts/release/supply-chain.mjs`, `tests/integration/release-supply-chain.test.mjs`, and the proposed new test. The canonical-inventory owner finished at 2e34a5f and current status is clean; if any required path is dirty at worker start, stop and report the collision rather than reset, stash, or edit over foreign work. Re-read archiveSource and cleanRoots: confirm the former still has an unguarded cleanup and the latter still catches and reports each cleanup failure; confirm no one has already created the focused test. Record a byte hash for the existing `tests/integration/release-supply-chain.test.mjs` because DoD requires it to remain unmodified. Confirm `typecheck:release`, `test:integration`, and Vitest's `tests/**/*.test.ts` include on current bytes. Capture the repo-wide baseline failure paths and exit codes before the diff by running each required leg separately (`pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm verify:foundation`, `pnpm verify:store`, and `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`); the daemon filter must show a nonzero executed-test count, never `No projects matched`. Do not commit logs or generated evidence.

TDD RED, WITH THE MINIMUM PRODUCTION TEST SEAM. In `archiveSource`, make the function a named export and add one optional dependency object whose sole override is `rmSync`; default it to the imported real `rmSync`. Do not add the catch yet, do not inject command/tar/git, and leave SYSTEM_PORTS calling archiveSource with one argument. Create `tests/integration/release-archive-cleanup.test.ts`, importing and exercising this production export. Build a tiny temporary Git repository using Node child-process/path/fs APIs (no shell-concatenated paths), commit one file, and use its real HEAD for archive success. Add four explicit named cases: (1) a throwing injected rmSync was attempted exactly once, is reported through a console.error spy, and the caller still receives the exact `{ destination, ok: true }`; (2) with a nonexistent repository root plus a pre-created `<destination>.tar`, the throwing injected rmSync was attempted/reported and the caller still receives the full exact refusal `{ code: "RELEASE_SUPPLY_CHAIN_REFUSED", ok: false, reason: "SOURCE_ARCHIVE_FAILED", refusedBy: "RELEASE_SUPPLY_CHAIN" }`; (3) default cleanup removes the real archive after success; and (4) default cleanup removes the pre-created archive after that exact refusal. Assert filesystem absence, not merely mock calls, in cases 3-4. Restore the console spy and recursively remove temporary roots with the test's real rmSync in finally/afterEach. Run only `pnpm exec vitest run tests/integration/release-archive-cleanup.test.ts`: all four tests must be discovered, and the two throwing-cleanup cases must fail because the current unguarded finally replaces their results.

MINIMUM FIX / GREEN. Change only archiveSource's finally block so the injected-or-default removal is attempted inside `try`, and on error calls `console.error(`release temporary cleanup failed: ${archive}: ${String(error)}`)` without rethrowing. Match cleanRoots' existing wording and subordinate-cleanup discipline; add at most a concise why-comment that cleanup reporting must not replace the already-computed archive result. Do not touch cleanRoots, SYSTEM_PORTS, release evidence, releaseRefusal, or any refusal vocabulary. The imported real rmSync remains the production default, including `{ force: true }`, so successful cleanup behavior is unchanged. Run the focused Vitest file once: require exactly four executed/passing tests, including literal code/reason/layer assertions for the refusal.

LOAD-BEARING MUTATION DRILL. Hash `scripts/release/supply-chain.mjs`, copy it to an out-of-repo temporary file, and install an EXIT trap that restores the bytes even if the drill command fails. Mutate exactly the new guarded finally back to the equivalent unguarded injected/default removal call (`finally { removeArchive(archive, { force: true }); }`), asserting exactly one replacement occurred. Run the two named `preserves ... when cleanup throws` tests and require a nonzero exit with both cases reported failed on the result-preservation assertions; a zero-test or zero-failure run is itself failure. Restore from the temporary copy, delete it, and compare the production file's SHA-256 to the pre-drill hash byte-for-byte before proceeding. Do not leave a probe, archive, transcript, or generated evidence file in the repository.

ONE FINAL VERIFICATION STEP. First re-run the five repo-wide legs from step 1 separately and compare their HEAD failing-path sets with the recorded baseline; the new failing-path delta intersected with this task's owned paths must be empty, and any foreign red must be quoted verbatim with exact paths. Confirm `git diff --name-only` is restricted to `scripts/release/supply-chain.mjs` plus the new focused test, the stored hash proves the existing release-supply-chain.test.mjs is unchanged, and the production source remains below 400 physical lines. Then run the exact completion-evidence command fresh in the foreground: `pnpm typecheck:release && pnpm test:integration`. It must exit 0; output must show the new focused file executed exactly four passing tests and the existing Node release suite executed a nonzero passing count. Preserve the command, exit code, and output tail for moe.complete_task.

FINAL ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, scoped only to this task's diff. Load `adversarial-self-review`; inspect `git diff -- scripts/release/supply-chain.mjs tests/integration/release-archive-cleanup.test.ts` as an attacker. Verify production callers cannot accidentally lose the real rmSync default, cleanup is attempted once on every success/refusal exit, an injected EBUSY cannot replace either exact result, reporter text follows cleanRoots, console spies and temporary Git/archive paths are always restored on test failure, refusal assertions pin code + reason + owning layer, and the happy refusal removal test starts with a real archive so absence is non-vacuous. Confirm no change to cleanRoots, evidence shape, refusal vocabulary, SYSTEM_PORTS, or the existing release test; no scratch files remain; and only explicit owned paths will be staged/committed. If any check fails, fix it and repeat the single final verification command before calling moe.complete_task.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Kept the fix in supply-chain.mjs rather than extracting a new production module: the file is already 257 lines but remains well below the mandatory 400-line split cap, and this narrow change must mirror cleanRoots in the same script. Rejected editing tests/integration/release-supply-chain.test.mjs because DoD requires that existing suite to remain byte-unmodified; a new Vitest .test.ts file is already discovered by tests/**/*.test.ts. Rejected reproducing Windows EBUSY with a held handle because it is race- and platform-dependent. Instead, expose only an optional rmSync dependency on the production archiveSource, exercise real git/tar against a tiny temporary repository, and inject the subordinate cleanup failure deterministically. Rejected a general command/system-port seam because the defect needs only rmSync injection and broader ports would increase production surface without value.

planningNotes.risks: Shared-tree safety is first: if supply-chain.mjs becomes dirty again, do not reset/stash or layer edits over it. Keep the optional dependency defaulted to the imported real rmSync so SYSTEM_PORTS and all production callers retain their one-argument behavior. Tests must use Node path APIs and a tiny temporary Git repository so Windows paths are not shell-quoted; restore console.error spies in finally and remove all temporary repositories/archives. For the refusal cleanup proof, pre-create destination.tar and use a nonexistent repository root so the original SOURCE_ARCHIVE_FAILED result is deterministic and default cleanup demonstrably removes a real file. The mutation drill must be guarded by an out-of-tree temporary backup/trap and a byte hash so no mutated or scratch evidence remains.
